target.title: fix(cron): keep valid command env vars when a sibling value is non-string (#105433)
target.body:
Fixes #105433

## What Problem This Solves

A command cron job whose `env` map contained a single non-string value silently lost its **entire** environment. For example, `env: { DEBUG: true, PATH: "/bin" }` sent to `cron.add`/`cron.update` was normalized down to no `env` at all — the valid `PATH` string was discarded alongside the invalid `DEBUG` boolean, before the Gateway ever validated the request. Operators got no error and no indication that their configured environment had vanished.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: `normalizeTrimmedStringRecord` in `src/cron/normalize.ts` returned `undefined` as soon as *any* entry was non-string, and the `env` branch treats `undefined` as "delete the whole field". So one bad value discarded every valid sibling.

The sibling helper in the same file, `normalizeTrimmedStringArray`, already handles this correctly: it filters invalid entries and only collapses to `undefined` when nothing valid remains. This change makes the record helper match that behavior — skip invalid entries, and only normalize the map away entirely when no valid entries survive.

Owner boundary: the fix stays inside the record normalizer that owns this semantic, mirroring the array normalizer right next to it. No caller, schema, or Gateway-validation change.

Non-goals: it does not change how an all-invalid or absent `env` is handled (still dropped/absent), and does not alter the Gateway request schema.

## User Impact

Valid cron command environment variables now survive when a sibling value is malformed, instead of the whole `env` map silently disappearing. Fully-valid `env` maps are unchanged (byte-for-byte).

## Evidence

Real behavior on current head `d80bbd782a01`, exercised through the actual `normalizeCronJobCreate` path with a command payload `env: { DEBUG: true, PATH: "/bin" }`:

Before fix:

~~~text
payload.env = null
PATH preserved?  false
~~~

After fix:

~~~text
payload.env = {"PATH":"/bin"}
PATH preserved?  true
~~~

- `vitest run src/cron/normalize.test.ts` (cron config) — 62 passed, including 2 new `#105433` regression tests (keeps valid sibling; drops the block only when no valid entries remain).
- Negative control: with the source fix stashed but the tests present, the "keeps valid env" test fails (`expected undefined to deeply equal { PATH: '/bin' }`) — proving the test actually guards this bug.
- `run-tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` — no errors.
- `oxfmt --check` on both touched files — clean.

AI-assisted (Claude Code); I have reviewed and understand every line.
